beats.text: Breaking Points, October twelfth. Seventeen minutes on the energy ceasefire. Here's what it was actually about.
beats.caption: Breaking Points · Oct 12 · 17:07

beats.text: Trump said: done. Delivered. The show said: nope. Not even close. And the whole segment ran right down the middle. Half noise, half signal. Forty-one lumens. That's how much light got through. Hold that number.
beats.caption: Declared +1.0 · Read −0.7 · Lumens 41

beats.text: Three lines did the work. One. Gregory Brew does the math. Three hundred thousand tons a month? That's seventy-four thousand barrels a day. We make three point six million. So, a rounding error. Cleanest line in the show.
beats.caption: Brew · “a few percent” · Dia 10, the cleanest read

beats.text: Two. The sanctions guys. Hours before the deal, Trump signed the Graham sanctions bill. And a license can't beat a law. That's not an opinion. That's a how-to-check.
beats.caption: Sanctions analysts · “a license can't override statute”

beats.text: Three. Krystal. He invented this ceasefire out of whole cloth. Same conclusion as Brew. She just got there through what she thinks of the guy.
beats.caption: Ball · “out of whole cloth” · Dia 78, read through the man

beats.text: And that's the gap. Everybody landed in the same place. Not delivered. The split isn't left versus right. It's how much of each line was about the deal, and how much was about the man.
beats.caption: The gap: same conclusion, different amounts of light

beats.text: Forty-one lumens. Less than half the light got through. The deal says three million tons by Christmas. We'll check in December.
beats.caption: Lumens 41 · the deal says 3M tons by year end

beats.text: That's the Diesel Deal, reduced. I'm Ted Turner. This is the Parallelogram Report.
beats.caption: theparallelogram.report
